landing.lead: GnomeVPN builds a tunnel to a node in another country. From the outside it looks like ordinary HTTPS. No logs, no ads, no traffic caps.

how.title: How it works
how.step1Body: Pay by card through YooKassa. From {price} ₽ a month, cancel in one click, no hidden charges.
how.step2Body: A free app from your own store: iPhone, Android, Windows, Linux, TV. We neither build it nor charge for it.
how.step3Body: One link from your account and the app fills up with every server in two flavours: the fast UDP one and a TCP fallback. The list keeps itself up to date.

features.title: What you get
features.protocolBody: Hysteria2 over QUIC leads, because it holds up better on mobile networks. Where UDP is blocked outright the list also carries a TCP fallback — one tap away.
features.devicesBody: Phone and computer at the same time on one subscription. Need more? Add them in your account.
features.platformsBody: iPhone, Android, Windows, Linux, Android TV and Apple TV. The same link works on all of them.
features.locationsBody: Switch country in one tap at no extra cost. New nodes appear in the app on their own.
features.noLogsBody: The server sees only how many bytes moved — enough to tell whether a node is alive. It is not tied to what you were doing.
features.openFormatBody: The subscription format is standard: paste it into Hiddify, Streisand or v2rayNG. You are locked into neither the app nor us.

privacy.title: Privacy Policy
privacy.intro: GnomeVPN is a VPN service built on the Hysteria2 protocol. It is designed to know as little about you as possible: browsing history is never collected and is physically stored nowhere.

collect.title: What we collect
collect.body: Only what the service cannot run without: an email address and a hashed password for signing in; subscription details such as the plan and its expiry; a device identifier the app generates itself, unrelated to any advertising ID; and the country you picked.

noLogs.title: Connection logs
noLogs.body: We keep no logs of your traffic. Visited addresses, DNS queries, connection contents and browsing history are never recorded. Nodes count transferred bytes only, which is how an active session is told apart from an abandoned one so device slots can be freed.

payments.title: Payments
payments.body: Payments are handled by YooKassa. Card details are processed by the payment provider — we never receive or store them. Our side keeps only the fact of payment, its amount, the subscription period and, if auto-renewal is on, the payment method identifier issued by YooKassa.

storage.title: Where data is stored
storage.body: Account data is stored on servers in Russia. Passwords are kept as irreversible hashes. Device and config records are removed together with the subscription or on your account deletion request.

thirdParty.title: Sharing with third parties
thirdParty.body: We do not sell or share your data. The exceptions are the payment provider needed to process a payment, and cases where disclosure is explicitly required by law.

rights.title: Your rights
rights.body: You can request a copy of your data, correct it, or delete your account entirely. Email us at the address below — requests are handled within 30 days.

children.title: Children
children.body: The service is not intended for anyone under 13. We do not knowingly collect data from children.

changes.title: Changes to this policy
changes.body: If this policy changes, the date at the top of the page is updated. Material changes are additionally announced to the email on your account.

faq.title: Frequently asked questions
faq.intro: The short answers to what people ask most. If yours is missing, email us.

whatIsIncy.q: What is INCY, and why that app?
whatIsIncy.a: INCY is a free client app that GnomeVPN runs through. It has no servers of its own: you paste a link from your account and the app fills up with our servers, your remaining traffic and your renewal date. We picked it because it exists on every platform, including iPhone and TVs, and has been debugged for years.

whyNotOwnApp.q: Why don't you ship your own app?
whyNotOwnApp.a: The honest answer: an app for five platforms means years of maintenance and a constant fight with app stores. INCY has already done that work. We put our effort into servers and speed instead of rewriting what already works. The subscription link stays yours — it works in other compatible clients too.

howToConnect.a: Three steps: install INCY from your store, copy the link from the App tab in your account, paste it into INCY. From there the app pulls the server list and keeps it up to date on its own.

whichProtocol.q: There are two servers per country — which one do I pick?
whichProtocol.a: Take the one without a tag: that is Hysteria2, faster and steadier on mobile. The entry marked "TCP" is for networks that block UDP — usually office Wi-Fi, hotels and some corporate networks. If the main one will not connect, switch to it.

howManyDevices.q: How many devices can I use?
howManyDevices.a: Two at once by default. There is one link per account — paste it on your phone, your laptop and your TV, but two connections run at a time. If you need more, buy extra devices in your account.

whichCountries.q: Which countries do you have servers in?
whichCountries.a: The list shows up in the app as soon as you add the link, and refreshes itself whenever we add a node. Switching country is one tap and costs nothing extra.

speed.a: We set no speed or traffic limits. Real speed depends on your own connection and how far the server is — the nearest one usually gives you close to your full line speed.

torrents.a: The tunnel passes them technically. Bear in mind that what you download stays your responsibility, and on some servers the hosting provider may send us a complaint — then we will ask you to switch location.

streaming.a: Usually yes, but we cannot promise it: streaming platforms block server addresses constantly. If one service refuses to open, try another country — that often fixes it.

notConnecting.q: The app will not connect. What now?
notConnecting.a: In order: check the subscription is active (INCY shows it), pull down to refresh the server list, try a different country. Still stuck? Rotate the link in your account and paste the new one. If that fails too, email us with a screenshot.

slowSpeed.q: It used to be fast and now it is slow
slowSpeed.a: Usually it is the server — try a neighbouring country. If every country is slow, test your speed without the VPN; sometimes it is the line itself. If it is fast without us and slow with us, write in and we will look at the node.

linkLeaked.q: My link reached the wrong hands
linkLeaked.a: Open your account, go to the App tab and press Rotate link. The old one stops working immediately. Then paste the new link again on each of your devices.

changePhone.q: I got a new phone — how do I move it over?
changePhone.a: Nothing to move. Install INCY on the new device and paste the same link from your account. If you are done with the old device, just delete the app there.

howToPay.a: By card on the site, through YooKassa. Access starts the moment the payment goes through, and the app picks up the new expiry date.

refund.a: Yes. If the service is not for you, email us within 14 days of paying and we will refund the unused period without an interrogation.

autoRenew.q: How do I turn off auto-renewal?
autoRenew.a: In your account, in the subscription block, with the Auto-renewal switch. Access stays until the end of the period you paid for; after that nothing is charged.

trial.a: There is no separate trial, but there is a 14-day refund — much the same thing, except you get full access from the start.

faq.stillStuck: Still stuck? Email us — we answer within a day.

setup.title: How to connect
setup.intro: GnomeVPN runs through INCY, a free app you install once. After that a single link from your account does the rest.

ios.name: iPhone and Mac
ios.install: Open the App Store and install INCY. The app is free and needs no account of its own.
ios.copyLink: Open your account on this site, go to the App tab and press Copy INCY link.
ios.import: Open INCY, tap + and choose import from clipboard. The app recognises the link and adds the subscription itself.
ios.connect: Pick a country from the list and press connect. The first time, iOS asks permission to add a VPN configuration — allow it.

android.name: Android
android.install: Install INCY from Google Play. If Play is unavailable, the INCY releases page has an APK.
android.copyLink: Open your account on this site, go to the App tab and press Copy INCY link.
android.import: In INCY tap + and import from the clipboard. Easier still: tap the link on the site — it opens the app and adds the subscription for you.
android.connect: Pick a country and connect. Android asks permission to set up a VPN connection — confirm it.

desktop.name: Windows, macOS and Linux
desktop.install: Download the installer above: exe for Windows, dmg for Mac, deb or rpm for Linux.
desktop.copyLink: Open your account in a browser, go to the App tab and copy the link.
desktop.import: Start INCY, press + and paste the link. Add it as a subscription rather than a single server, so the server list keeps updating itself.
desktop.connect: Pick a country and connect. On Windows you will be asked to approve an elevation prompt — it is needed to create the network adapter.

tv.name: TV
tv.install: On Android TV install INCY from Google Play; on Apple TV from the App Store.
tv.copyLink: Typing the link on a TV remote is no fun: open your account on your phone and show the QR code on the App tab.
tv.import: In INCY on the TV choose to add a subscription and scan the QR code from your phone screen.
tv.connect: Pick a country and connect. From then on the tunnel comes up by itself when the TV turns on.

meta.title: About
meta.description: Why GnomeVPN runs on Hysteria2 and QUIC, how the infrastructure works and what we do not store.

about.title: About the service
about.intro: Short and without the marketing: how this works inside and why we made these choices.

problem.title: The problem we set out to solve
problem.body: Classic TCP-based VPN protocols stopped working reliably in Russia. Carrier equipment learned to recognise the characteristic start of a connection and cut it a few minutes into real traffic. Changing port or server helps only briefly.

protocol.title: Why Hysteria2
protocol.body: Hysteria2 runs over QUIC, which means UDP, and from the outside it looks like an ordinary HTTP/3 website. UDP traffic is inspected differently from TCP, and in practice such a tunnel survives noticeably longer. QUIC also handles packet loss better, so speed holds up on mobile networks.

noLogs.title: What we do not store
noLogs.body: We keep no record of your connections: which sites you opened, which address you connected from, or when. Servers see how many bytes moved — that is how we tell whether a node is alive, and it is not tied to what you were doing.

infrastructure.title: Infrastructure
infrastructure.body: Nodes are rented from several providers in different countries, each set up automatically from the same script. When a node stops answering it drops out of the list in the app on its own, with nothing for you to do.

client.title: About the app
client.body: The client is INCY — a free third-party app that we do not develop. That is the honest arrangement: rather than spend years chasing someone else's feature set on five platforms, we hand you a standard subscription link. It works in other compatible clients too — you are not locked in.

honesty.title: What we do not promise
honesty.body: We do not promise it will work everywhere forever: blocking changes, and sometimes nodes have to change with it. We do not promise anonymity — a VPN hides traffic from your ISP, it does not make you invisible. If the service is not for you, we refund within 14 days.
